doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What aggravates him; young players and what he has learned since
summary: He dislikes outsiders announcing they are playing jazz, praises young players such as Isaiah, and looks back on what he learned from Bucky.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Just to wrap up, do you have any things, I guess musically, that aggravate you?

Yeah. I mean there’s one — there was a — the thing I think one thing that aggravates me, it’s like when people from outside of the genre — and I don’t mean musicians, but like actors or something and there’s like the thing where they go, I’m going to play jazz now and everybody goes, oh it’s so cool it’s this famous person is playing jazz. And you go well I heard what you did and I feel like I have some sort of knowledge of what jazz is. And that’s fine but there are so many other people I could be watching right now. And so I don’t want to —
I know who you’re talking about. At least two or three people, yes.

And so you know that kind of thing, but I mean the good news is is there’s a lot of great music out there. There’s a lot of kids who now can learn in high school and in college from real live great teachers of jazz. I mean a guy like Isaiah, they — you know Isaiah and Mike, and Mike’s a product of the New School I think, too. And Isaiah out of Juilliard. And they’ll sit and they’ll sing choruses on these records they listen to. I make it sound like these records they listen to — but they’re so immersed in it. And my thing was more Bucky Pizzarelli led me down a Bucky Pizzarelli path. There was Benny Goodman, Count Basie, and Zoot Sims was our guy. So you know I was very loyal to the circle. And then there’s the Joe Mooney records and then the Nat Cole records. So but I mean I was never really outside of that circle. But I’m learning more from sitting with this 26- year-old kid who is so fantastic, going, “Have you heard this Gerald Wilson record?” Have you heard this other thing, you know here’s even just Phineas Newborn records that I, you know, heard in passing. And you know going on car rides with this guy, it’s like a master class. Don’t give me a test. But that’s the good news. So rather than think about the things that upset me, there’s not that much. I’m just happy that we’re out there. So it did take 33 years to sort of feel comfortable where you’re at you know, so since the last time I’ve managed to keep doing what we’re doing. We make decent money and the organization has gotten better. The fun thing is I’ve been able to look back at these things, these reviews and it’s fun to think about all the work that — you know and you hear all the things that I learned in my 20s from Bucky and into my 30s I have all, one way or another as you’ve heard in the last hour it’s been something that there was all that information. So the good news is I paid attention so that when I got my picture with Rosemary Clooney it was a good experience. You know, I earned the things, the places I got to be because I paid attention and that was the key.
